chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from some of our companions, from some of them, upon them be peace, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered into the state of Ihram wearing two garments of Kursuf.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family
key_terms.كُرْسُفٍ: Kursuf (a specific type of fine, woven fabric)

ai.seo_question: What clothing did the Prophet wear when entering the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) adherence to simplicity and modesty during the sacred state of Ihram, specifically noting the use of Kursuf, a fine linen or cotton fabric. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a key precedent for the permissibility of wearing two separate, unstitched garments during pilgrimage, distinguishing it from the prohibition of sewn clothing. The emphasis on 'two garments' underscores the minimalistic requirement for Ihram attire, reflecting the spiritual purity and equality of the pilgrim before God.
